description:
Collisions and Conservation of Linear Momentum
Exp. ME-3
Purpose
The purpose of this experiment is to verify the conservation of linear momentum in collisions between
two pucks on a level air table, which together form an isolated system. The motion of the center of mass
of the two pucks is followed through the collision, and the kinetic energy before and after the collision
is compared for an elastic and for a completely inelastic collision.
Introduction
The linear momentum of an object of mass m moving with velocity⃗ v is defined as
⃗
P = m⃗ v. (3.1)
An object at rest therefore has zero momentum, and an object of constant mass changes its momentum
only when its velocity changes, that is, only when a net external force acts on it. For a system of several
particles, the forces the particles exert on one another cancel in pairs, so the total momentum⃗ Ptot =
⃗
P1 +⃗ P2 + · · · +⃗ PN responds only to forces from outside the system. When there is no such net external
force, the system is called isolated, and its total momentum stays constant in time no matter what
collisions take place among its particles.
In this experiment the system is two pucks on a level air table. With the table horizontal and the friction
almost eliminated by the air cushion, the pucks experience no net external force, so we expect their total
momentum to be the same before and after they collide. The dots produced on the data sheet by such
a collision are shown in Fig. 3.1(a).
